title: Disagreement, the most-asked question: two traps, one good shape
takeaway: A disagreement story scores when evidence settled it and your own position moved at least partly.
sources: The single most-asked behavioural question in engineering.
Two traps: picking a disagreement where you were obviously right and they were obviously stupid, and picking one where you simply caved.
The good version is a real technical disagreement resolved through evidence, ideally where your position shifted at least partly.

cells.label: You were obviously right
cells.note: Trap: they were obviously stupid and you held firm

cells.label: You simply caved
cells.note: Trap: your position moved, but nothing settled it

cells.label: Settled by evidence
cells.note: The good version, short of the ideal: your position did not shift

cells.label: Evidence, and your view shifted
cells.note: The good version: evidence, and your position shifted at least partly
